text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Television appearances of woman who claims to have been pressured into sex with Islamist sect members break ratings records.
- Former parliamentary speaker Husamettin Cindoruk forms a new conservative opposition party.
- Repentant far-left killer of industrialist put under protection in jail in fear of attack by former militant colleagues.
- Dutch authorities freezes the accounts of Turkish bank representatives in the Netherlands because of money-laundering accusations.
- Islamist-led government plans extra wage rises of 20 percent on average for police after promising similar increases for military.
- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash criticises Turkey for not acting quick enough to halt Russian missile sale to Cyprus.
- Large increase in car exports in 1996.
- Parliamentary commission investigating security scandal runs up against brick walls.
